items.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI will be, barring some sort of disaster, the biggest piece of media released in 2026. Doctor Doom, eat your cold, stony little heart out.

It’s practically guaranteed to be the largest game launch in years, possibly ever…despite being limited to an Xbox and PlayStation debut. The game is inevitably coming to PC later — like its fictional criminal heroes, Rockstar’s not going to leave that kind of money on the table. But how long will it take? That’s the question I’m pondering in this week’s newsletter.

items.title: How to reinstall Windows and give your PC a fresh start
items.description: Once upon a time, “reinstalling Windows” was an often recommended remedy for all sorts of computer problems. Windows 95 and XP were notorious for becoming less stable over time, with “crap in the machine” in the form of settings left in the Registry, traces of uninstalled programs that had not been properly removed, and other things that lurked. Indeed, many people chose to reinstall from time to time even if the computer showed no symptoms, as part of regular maintenance.

items.title: Best SSDs: From SATA to PCIe 5.0, from budget to premium
items.description:
Solid state drives, or SSDs, are singularly responsible for vast improvements to PC performance over the last decade or so. Taking the place of mechanical hard drives, SSDs transformed once-ponderous boot times into being virtually instantaneous, programs and games are far more responsive, and the frustratingly long large-file loads are largely a thing of a past.

If you’re not yet using an SSD, you are missing out. If you already have an older SSD, you might consider upgrading it for the even speedier performance offered by cutting-edge PCIe 4.0 and 5.0 designs — if your PC sports those technologies, of course.
